mcqs.question: A force of 500 N is applied uniformly on a surface having an area of 0.02 m². What is the stress produced on the material?
mcqs.explanation: Stress is defined as the internal restoring force per unit area, σ = F/A. Here σ = 500 N / 0.02 m² = 25,000 N/m² = 25,000 Pa. Option A results from dividing by 0.05 m² (incorrect area). Option C mistakenly multiplies force and area. Option D uses the force value directly without dividing by area. Hence, B is correct.

mcqs.question: When a uniform tensile force is applied along the length of a cylindrical rod, the internal stress acting on any cross‑section perpendicular to the rod is called:
mcqs.explanation: Longitudinal stress arises when a force is applied parallel to the axis of a body, producing normal stress on cross‑sections perpendicular to the force. Shear stress acts parallel to the surface, bulk stress is hydrostatic, and torsional stress is due to twisting. Therefore, option C correctly identifies longitudinal stress.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes bulk stress from longitudinal stress in a solid?

options.A: Bulk stress acts on a surface parallel to the applied force, while longitudinal stress acts on a surface perpendicular to the force.
options.B: Bulk stress is defined as force per unit area on any face of a body under hydrostatic pressure, whereas longitudinal stress is force per unit area on a cross‑section due to axial loading.
options.C: Bulk stress involves shear forces, whereas longitudinal stress involves normal forces.
options.D: Bulk stress is always larger than longitudinal stress for the same magnitude of force.

mcqs.answer: Bulk stress is defined as force per unit area on any face of a body under hydrostatic pressure, whereas longitudinal stress is force per unit area on a cross‑section due to axial loading.
mcqs.explanation: Bulk (or hydrostatic) stress acts equally in all directions on all faces of a body under uniform pressure, and it is normal to the surface. Longitudinal stress results from an axial force and acts on the cross‑section perpendicular to that force. Option A reverses the orientation, C incorrectly labels bulk stress as shear, and D is not generally true. Hence, B is the correct distinction.

mcqs.question: A solid circular shaft of radius 0.05 m transmits a torque of 120 N·m. What is the maximum tangential (shear) stress on the shaft? (Use τ = T·r / J, where J = πr⁴/2 for a solid shaft.)
mcqs.explanation: First compute the polar moment of inertia: r = 0.05 m, r⁴ = (0.05)⁴ = 6.25 × 10⁻⁶ m⁴. J = πr⁴/2 = (π × 6.25 × 10⁻⁶)/2 ≈ 9.82 × 10⁻⁶ m⁴. The shear stress τ = T·r / J = (120 N·m × 0.05 m) / 9.82 × 10⁻⁶ m⁴ ≈ 6.1 × 10⁵ N/m² = 6.1 × 10⁵ Pa. Option B matches this value. Options A, C, and D arise from arithmetic errors such as using an incorrect J or missing the factor of 0.5.
